subject: giant isopod
title: This Deep-Sea Bug Refused Every Meal for Five Years, and Lived

scenes.text: An aquarium animal refused every meal for five years. And it looked perfectly fine.
Giant Isopod Number One, a foot-long deep-sea scavenger, last ate on January 2, 2009.
Keepers in Japan tried new foods, warmer water, even pressing food to its face. It only pretended to chew.
In the wild, they wait on the seafloor for dead whales and fish to sink.
It died on Valentine's Day 2014, after 1,868 days. No blockage. Nobody knows why it stopped.

description:
A giant isopod at Japan's Toba Aquarium refused food for more than five years.
Giant Isopod No. 1, about 30 cm long and over 2 pounds, last ate a nibble of horse mackerel on 2 January 2009. Keepers changed its food and water temperature and pressed food against its face; it went through the motions of eating but never took a bite. It was found dead on 14 February 2014, after 1,868 days without a meal. A dissection found no blockage.
How long do you think you could go without eating?
first_comment: The other giant isopods in the same aquarium ate normally the whole time. Why do you think this one stopped?
